title: The Lock Call: Monday, November 23

lines.text: [excited] Merv and I are on opposite sides of the same game tonight!
[grinning] And the president found somebody to blame for the stock market. Eight picks. Go!
From The Window at Hardwood Bricks, this is Tops and Bottoms, the Lock Call. I'm Leslie Phyllis.
And I'm Brett Busberger. Leslie, the president says the market is down more than six trillion dollars, and it's all because the Democrats won the midterms.
His words: the Democrats are bad. [laughs] Honey, when my over loses, I don't blame the voters.
[grumbling] He's right. I was red hot until November third.
[dry] You're four and four, Edwin. That's not the midterms. That's you.
Today's picks. I'm all in on one game: U N C Greensboro at Pepperdine. Over one fifty-five and a half, and Pepperdine laying ten and a half.
The machine likes Denver, plus thirty-six and a half at Kansas. And Wright State, laying two against Akron.
And I have Akron, plus two. Somebody at this table is wrong, young man. Plus the under, one fifty-four and a half, V C U and Providence.
[out of breath] North Florida, plus eight and a half at home. And the under, one sixty-four and a half. Somebody painted over the seven in my elevator. Don't ask.
The board. Last night the house went seven and one. Leslie, Merv and me, all two and oh.
Which keeps me on top. Seven and one, up five point three seven units. Merv's six and two. Brett's five and three.
And Edwin is four and four.
That's the Lock Call. The picks column is up now at hardwood bricks dot com.
Twenty-one and up. If gambling's a problem, call one eight hundred GAMBLER.
Keep it mid. Keep it real.

news.item: On Truth Social on Nov 22, President Trump wrote that the market is down more than 6 trillion dollars since the Democrats' Nov 3 midterm win and that this is "100% due to the fact that the Democrats are 'BAD'." The figures are his claims.

notes.board: Standings through Nov 22; yesterday = Nov 22 card (house 7-1).

blurb: Brett and Merv take opposite sides of Akron and Wright State, the president finds someone to blame for the stock market, and Edwin tries the same excuse.
